title: Geometric quotient filtrations give Weil composition series
statement: Fix finite-field and coefficient data $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k_0$, and $\Qlb=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ [d-real-setup]. Let $C_0/k_0$ be a smooth geometrically connected separated finite-type curve in the sense of [d-real-setup], put $C=(C_0)_k$, and choose a geometric generic point $\bar\eta$. Let $\mathcal H$ be a classical lisse Weil sheaf [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves; def-wf-fundamental-representation] on $C_0$ with a given finite filtration $0=\mathcal H_0\subset\cdots\subset\mathcal H_r=\mathcal H$ by lisse Weil subsheaves. Assume each quotient $\mathcal T_j=\mathcal H_j/\mathcal H_{j-1}$ is nonzero and its underlying local system on $C$ is irreducible, meaning that its stalk representation of $P=\pi_1(C,\bar\eta)$ has no nonzero proper invariant subspace. Under the Weil fundamental representation of [def-wf-fundamental-representation], the given sheaf filtration gives a composition series of the finite-dimensional representation $V=\mathcal H_{\bar\eta}$ of $W=W(C_0,\bar\eta)$ [def-real-weil-representation-operations; def-mg-weil-composition-series]. More precisely, each inclusion gives a $W$-stable subspace, successive representation quotients are canonically $\mathcal T_{j,\bar\eta}$ with their prescribed Weil action, and each is an irreducible $W$-representation. Thus every prescribed quotient is a constituent of $\mathcal H$ in the representation-theoretic sense. The assertion includes $r=0$ and does not require $\mathcal H$ to be semisimple or the filtration to split.

proof.text: Use the normalized realization functor and its Hom dictionary [new-p6-etale-weil-realization; new-p6-etale-weil-fiber-hom] on the connected geometric curve. Its arrows are the actual prescribed stalk maps, so they are equivariant and preserve identities and composition. Full faithfulness of its composite with the full inclusion into Rep identifies a sheaf as zero exactly when its stalk is a subsingleton: a zero source makes the identity of its image the zero endomorphism by fullness, and zero reflection is standard full-faithful reflection. Finite dimension follows from etaleFundamentalRep_isLAdic [def-wf-fundamental-representation]. The supplied stalk exactness, specialized to the chosen point, already gives injectivity and surjectivity, without using the full exact tensor equivalence. Reverse induction along the finite diagram gives injectivity of every map to its last term. Let F_i be the image subrepresentation of that map, with LinearEquiv.ofInjective identifying the original stalk with F_i. Functoriality gives monotonicity, the initial zero stalk gives F_0=0 and the last identity gives F_r=V.

proof.text: For each quotient q_j, transport its actual equivariant stalk map to F_{j+1} using the inverse image identification. Its kernel is the comap of F_j along the subtype, by the given exactness and the injectivity into V. The first isomorphism theorem for the transported surjective linear map yields F_{j+1}/F_j equivalent to the prescribed quotient stalk. Check equivariance on quotient representatives; the resulting equivalence satisfies exactly [e_{j+1}(v)] maps to q_j(v). Restrict any Weil-stable subspace of a quotient to the geometric subgroup using the defining restriction identity of etaleFundamentalRep [def-wf-fundamental-representation]. The assumed geometric irreducibility forces it to be zero or the whole stalk; zero reflection and the nonzero quotient hypothesis give a nontrivial stalk. Thus every prescribed quotient representation is irreducible.

proof.text: Transfer irreducibility across the quotient equivalences. Subrepresentation.isIrreducible_subquotient_iff makes each adjacent pair a cover. Construct the RelSeries with length exactly r and the image chain, and its Representation.CompositionSeries with the proved zero and top endpoints [def-mg-weil-composition-series]. The stalk equivalences have the required ambient-inclusion formula by construction. Each prescribed quotient is a constituent by isConstituent_of_equiv_subquotient applied to the inverse quotient equivalence [def-real-weil-representation-operations]. All constructions also apply at r=0: reverse induction starts with the last identity, the sole image is simultaneously zero and top, and all factor conclusions have empty index type. No splitting or semisimplicity enters.
